mappings.rationale: Minimize the place-value weighted sum by putting the smallest digits in the hundreds places, then the tens places, and exhibit an attaining arrangement.
mappings.answerReason: An exchange of digits lowers the sum whenever a larger digit occupies a higher-weight place. Thus hundreds use 4 and 5, tens use 6 and 7, and units use 8 and 9, giving 900 + 130 + 17 = 1047.

mappings.answerReason: Changing the tenths digit gives 0.92345. Every other permitted change leaves the tenths digit equal to 1, so each produces a smaller number.

mappings.rationale: Determine possible square residues modulo 10 by squaring the possible units digits.
mappings.answerReason: Squaring digits 0 through 9 gives units digits 0, 1, 4, 9, 6, 5, 6, 9, 4, 1. Therefore 8 cannot be the units digit of a whole-number square.
